notes:
- Retention is calmer. Its cuts are planned around the footage's own: never a few frames off one of the recording's camera cuts or jump cuts (a cutaway ends on the recording's own cut instead), B-roll covers the jump cuts, the speaker holds at least 1.6 s between cutaways and each cutaway runs 1.2 to 2.2 s.
- Retention's punch-in changes only on a jump cut no B-roll covers, instead of flipping on every speaker shot, and its words stay on one line for the whole clip instead of moving to each shot's face.
- A close-up is never treated as a wide shot because someone stands behind the speaker (a close-up with a body behind it could be read as a wide, and its captions went above the head).
